title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: generative-AI skills in Create for GCC and GCC High
summary: Hold: the cost rating describes indirect costs only even though the briefing correctly identifies an add-on licence requirement. The roadmap facts, licence requirement and documented control paths are supported; the governance checklist also names controls missing from the table.

claims.claim: The Create article describes user-initiated creation from a description or template, not an autonomous agent.
claims.quote: Select what you'd like to create ... Enter a description of what you want to create or select a template to start.

claims.claim: A low cost rating represents the documented add-on licensing requirement and licence assignment costs.
claims.quote: cost: "low"; licensing.model: "add-on"; "Microsoft's service description says AI-powered features in Create need a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, an add-on plan." The scale defines low as indirect cost only and medium as add-on licences for a subset.
claims.fix: Set cost to "medium" and replace the cost rationale with: "Medium. AI-powered features in Create require the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence for the users who need them; the Create article names no separate meter. Admin setup adds indirect cost."

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks administrators to configure or take stock of has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Before rollout asks readers to "Create a mail-enabled security group" and "Create an organisation assets library to connect to Copilot"; the table contains only licence assignment, two brand-kit policies and the individual-feature-switch gap.
claims.fix: The Before rollout steps for creating the two mail-enabled security groups and the organisation assets library have no matching controls-table rows. Remove those two checklist bullets; retain the already-supported prerequisite statements in Cost and licensing.
